forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Mansfield Council carries forward £33.8m of capital investment to next year as major projects slip.
news_drafts.lead: Mansfield Council is deferring £33.8 million of planned capital spending from 2026/27 to 2027/28, with only 66 per cent of its General Fund capital programme forecast to be delivered this year. The carry-forwards — £26.8 million from the General Fund and £7 million from the Housing Revenue Account, which funds the council's own housing stock — reflect delays across major projects including the Mansfield Connect digital transformation programme, which is forecast to spend only £1 million of a £23.7 million budget, and the White Hart Street housing development, which is expected to deliver only £2.3 million of its £9.3 million allocation. The council's revenue budget, however, is broadly on track, with a £169,000 surplus forecast for the year. Interest income is running £300,000 ahead of budget due to higher-than-expected rates, offsetting pressures from higher-than-budgeted vacancies in housing stock and unmet savings targets across 15 service areas.

news_drafts.headline: Mansfield Council borrows £15m in quarter with half its debt due within a year
news_drafts.lead: Mansfield Council borrowed £15m in the first three months of 2026/27 and expects to raise £50m more this year, taking total debt toward £135m. Nearly half its existing borrowing—£46.8m of £98.8m—matures within 12 months, forcing the council to refinance at short notice. The council is betting that interest rates will fall to limit refinancing costs, but early repayment charges on its £52.7m Public Works Loan Board debt are so expensive that it cannot reschedule loans if rates hold steady or rise. Treasury management papers show investment income is running £300,000 above budget because base rates remained at 3.75% longer than forecast, but this benefit is temporary and will reverse if rates fall as expected.

findings.headline: Capital programme carrying forward £33.798m (32% of approved budget) to 2027/28 due to slippage.
findings.detail: The capital programme shows significant slippage, with £26.780m of General Fund capital and £7.018m of HRA capital (totalling £33.798m) forecast to be carried forward to 2027/28, representing approximately 32% of the approved £106.398m budget. The paper notes the slippage has affected both General Fund and HRA but does not explain its causes.
findings.matters: Substantial capital slippage may indicate underlying delivery challenges such as procurement delays, planning issues, or contractor availability problems that could persist into future years.
findings.figures: £26.780m GF carry-forward, £7.018m HRA carry-forward, £106.398m approved budget
findings.quote: There has been slippage in the capital programme, which has affected both the General Fund and Housing Revenue Account.

findings.headline: Section 24 Direction from Local Government Reorganisation will restrict Mansfield's financial autonomy from late 2026.
findings.detail: Local Government Reorganisation is proceeding with Option 1Bii selected as the preferred structure. When the Structural Changes Order is published towards the end of 2026, the Secretary of State will issue a Section 24 Direction that will prevent the council from making significant financial commitments without the consent of the incoming shadow authority. The council explicitly states this will directly impact its financial decisions.
findings.matters: Restrictions on financial autonomy create uncertainty around the council's ability to make borrowing decisions, capital commitments, or respond to emerging financial pressures independently.
findings.quote: At the same time, the Secretary of State will also issue a Section 24 Direction, which will prevent outgoing predecessor councils from making significant financial commitments without the consent of the incoming shadow authority. This will directly impact the financial decisions that Mansfield District Council can take.

findings.headline: Mansfield forecasts £3.151m deficit in 2027/28 to be covered by reserve drawdown.
findings.detail: The updated medium-term financial plan identifies a deficit of £3.151m in 2027/28, driven by a significant decrease in business rates funding due to the reset of the business rates system. The council plans to use its NNDR (business rates) earmarked reserve to balance this deficit, with the arrangement to be reviewed during the 2027/28 budget-setting process.
findings.matters: A deficit covered by reserve drawdown is not sustainable long-term; if the underlying budget problem is not resolved, reserves will deplete and the council will face financial pressure in subsequent years.
findings.quote: It is recommended that the NNDR reserve set aside for this purpose is utilised to balance the deficit in 2027/28. This will be reviewed as part of the 2027/28 budget-setting process.

findings.headline: General Fund forecast to achieve £1.260m surplus in 2026/27, increasing reserves to £3.385m.
findings.detail: The council is forecasting a surplus of £1.260m on its 2026/27 revenue budget, which will increase General Fund balances from £2.125m to £3.385m. This surplus is £1.285m above the minimum level of balances approved for the year, providing financial headroom.
findings.matters: A strong reserve position improves the council's financial resilience and ability to manage future pressures or unexpected costs.
findings.figures: £1.260m surplus forecast, opening balance £2.125m, projected closing balance £3.385m, £1.285m above minimum
findings.quote: At the end of the financial year, the General Fund is forecast to achieve a surplus position against its budget of £1.260m, which will increase the level of General Fund balances available.

findings.headline: External Wall Insulation scheme discontinued; £200k budget reallocated to other housing assistance.
findings.detail: The council has cancelled its External Wall Insulation programme and reallocated the £200k budget: £87,265 to Discretionary Assistance and £112,735 to Healthy Homes Grant. The scheme is noted as 'no longer to be completed'. This represents a policy decision to cease this capital programme and redirect resources.
findings.matters: Programme cancellations can indicate either policy shifts or practical delivery constraints. Discontinuing an energy efficiency programme may reflect funding pressures, procurement difficulties, or reprioritization, all of which are relevant to understanding the council's capital strategy and financial flexibility.
findings.figures: EWI budget cancelled £200,000; reallocated to Discretionary Assistance £87,265; Healthy Homes Grant £112,735
findings.quote: EWI not being offered this year budget to be used to fund other assistance
